newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB gains as analysts upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB gains as analysts upgrade.

text.p: Shares in Lloyds TSB Group Plc rose on Thursday, defying the weak tone elsewhere in the UK equity market, as three top brokerages upgraded their ratings and earnings estimates on the stock, dealers said.
Lloyds shares were up 12p to 617-1/2 by 0944 GMT in active trade of 9.1 million shares, making it the second most active stock in the market overall.
Dealers said the upgrades came after Lloyds held analyst briefings on its current trading performance, before the end of the first half of the year.

Analysts at SBC Warburg upgraded the stock to "buy" from "hold" and raised their 1997 pre-tax profit estimate to 3,108 million stg from 2,935 million, sources said. For 1998 their raised to 3,625 million stg from 3,367 million.
At ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, analyst Peter Toeman raised his 1997 pre-tax profit forecast to 3.2 billion stg from 3.1 billion and repeated an "undervalued" rating on the shares.
Merrill Lynch raised its recommendation on Lloyds to a long and short-term "buy" from a long and short-term "accumulate."
Merrill also nudged up its earnings forecasts for 1997 and 1998, citing improved margins, strength in Lloyds' mortgage business and costs savings from its merger with TSB.
For 1997 it raised to 3,162 million stg from 2,926 million and for 1998 it raised to 3,573 million stg from 3,202 million, sources said.
Analysts at Merrill were not immediately available for comment.
